newsitem.title: POLAND: AUDITORS UNCOVER "ILLEGAL" POLISH CABINET FUND.
newsitem.headline: AUDITORS UNCOVER "ILLEGAL" POLISH CABINET FUND.

text.p: Polish official auditors have uncovered one million marks, kept illegally on a Cabinet Office account and partly held by the country's Berlin mission, which was not listed in the budget, their spokesman said on Tuesday.
Przemyslaw Szustakiewicz told Reuters the Supreme Auditing Chamber (NIK) found the money during a routine check on implementation of the 1996 budget by the Cabinet Office.

"The money was on two accounts: some 650,000 marks was on an account in the Pekao SA bank and 311,000 marks was on an account of the Polish diplomatic mission in Berlin -- together with other small cash it was about one million marks," he said.

"We conclude that it is illegal and pointless for the Cabinet Office to keep funds outside the budget, treating them as own funds, over which there is no parliamentary control," said Szustakiewicz of NIK, a powerful watchdog overseeing government spending.
The revelation prompted Polish news media to question the purpose of what was quickly dubbed a "secret" fund.
Szustakiewicz said that in 1996 the Cabinet Office had spent only 7,000 marks of the money for dentists equipment for its clinic.

"I don't know where the money came from, but in our opinion spending it was illegal because under the budget law state institutions cover their expenses from the budget and return their revenues also to the budget," Szustakiewicz said.
"The Cabinet Office, on the other hand, says that funds in foreign currencies are not subject to the budget law, but we disagree with that interpretation," he said.
He said the matter would now have to be resolved by the parliamentary budget committee and parliament when it votes on approving the realisation of the 1996 budget.
The government press office had no immediate comment.
